title: Kinetic Lifshitz invariants and dynamics of nonreciprocal fluctuations in superconductors
authors: Tony Liu, Joaquim Telles de Miranda, Daniel Shaffer, Alex Levchenko
abstract: We derive the generalized time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory of a disordered noncentrosymmetric superconductor from the Keldysh nonlinear sigma model, using a two-dimensional electron gas with Rashba spin-orbit coupling and an in-plane Zeeman field as a minimal model. On the thermodynamic side we construct the Lifshitz invariants of the free energy, the linear and cubic gradient terms and the momentum-odd part of the quartic vertex, and trace their dependence on disorder. These couplings are governed by a single closed-form kernel controlled by the ratio of the Dyakonov-Perel spin-relaxation rate to temperature, interpolating between the weak-relaxation regime, where the invariants are suppressed, and the relaxation-dominated regime, where the helical modulation of the order parameter saturates at a universal, disorder-independent value. This crossover reconciles conflicting results for the magnetoelectric couplings of dirty Rashba superconductors. Because the theory is formulated on the Keldysh contour, it also determines the dissipative dynamics: the relaxation rate of a fluctuation with pair momentum $\mathbf{q}$, and hence, by the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, the Langevin noise power, acquires a term odd in $\mathbf{q}$ and odd in the magnetic field. The structure of this kinetic Lifshitz invariant is dictated by Onsager reciprocity: friction and noise renormalize in lockstep, so equal-time fluctuations remain Gibbsian while the dynamics are nonreciprocal. As applications we compute the superconducting diode efficiency near $T_c$, where the cubic invariant competes with the quartic vertex and with even higher-gradient terms rendered odd by the helical shift, reversing the sign of the diode coefficient, and the fluctuation-induced magnetochiral anisotropy above $T_c$, where the current-resolved nonreciprocal resistance forms a plateau across the Gaussian regime.
summary: This work develops a generalized time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory for disordered, noncentrosymmetric superconductors using the Keldysh formalism. It determines that nonreciprocal Lifshitz invariants appear in both the free energy and the dynamic fluctuation terms. The results unify conflicting theoretical predictions by introducing a single crossover function controlling the system's response to disorder.
main_problem: The study derives a generalized time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory for disordered noncentrosymmetric superconductors, focusing on the appearance of Lifshitz-type nonreciprocal couplings in the quantum (Keldysh) sector.
main_result: The kinetic Lifshitz invariants are governed by a single crossover kernel dependent on the ratio of the spin-relaxation rate to temperature, reconciling previous conflicting results for magnetoelectric couplings.
method: The theory is derived from the Keldysh nonlinear sigma model and utilizes principles like the Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem (FDT) and Onsager reciprocity to determine dynamics.
model_or_system: The minimal model is a disordered noncentrosymmetric superconductor realized via a two-dimensional electron gas with Rashba spin-orbit coupling and an in-plane Zeeman field. The analysis uses the Keldysh formalism to construct the effective action.
key_observables: Superconducting diode efficiency, fluctuation-induced magnetochiral anisotropy, relaxation rate of fluctuations ($\mathbf{q}$ dependence), and Langevin noise power (which acquire $\mathbf{q}$-odd and $B$-field odd terms).
important_parameters: The ratio of the Dyakonov-Perel spin-relaxation rate ($\Gamma_t$) to temperature ($T$), which dictates the crossover between weak-relaxation and relaxation-dominated regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the diffusive regime and relies on gauge covariance arguments within the Keldysh formalism.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general context of Lifshitz invariants, applies this to superconductors using the Keldysh NLSM, derives the full dynamical theory (TDGL equation), and computes specific nonreciprocal couplings in various limits defined by $\Gamma_t/T$.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of fluctuation-dissipation theorems and symmetry principles (Onsager reciprocity) to derive non-equilibrium dynamics in a superconducting context provides advanced tools for understanding dissipation beyond simple mean-field treatments.
